title: Changing pool parameters at run time
context: How can you change a ThreadPoolExecutor's size or queue at run time?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: ThreadPoolExecutor has setCorePoolSize and setMaximumPoolSize, which apply on the next task. The queue can't be resized in place, so you replace the executor, or use a custom queue whose capacity you can change, such as a wrapper around LinkedBlockingDeque. Expose the values through configuration or JMX, and log each change. Growing the core size starts threads lazily, so a change does not take effect for running work immediately.

points.title: Setters exist for sizes
points.why: setCorePoolSize and setMaximumPoolSize change limits without a restart.

points.title: Queue capacity is fixed
points.why: The queue's capacity is set when it is built, so changing it needs a new pool or a custom queue.
